en: But that ain't gonna work if we're talking about a housewife's grocery shoppin' though. Ya can't cook nothin' if ya ain't got the groceries.
In that case, plan your budget in advance. That way you can buy what you want, and if you stay within that budget, you'll be fine.
Hey, that makes sense! You're real money-smart, Kiryu-san! Ya'd even be a better housewife than me!
Let's just say I've been with someone who was very keen on household finances.
Go with your gut. If something really grabs your attention, that probably means you subconsciously know you really need it.
Are y'sure? But like, what if somethin' catches my eye by coincidence? Like, what if it's something totally weird?
The shops have already done the thinking for you. They arrange sale items so that the best sellers are right in front for you to see.
They really do that? So then how come I keep buyin' stupid stuff despite all that?
I reckoned that since y'were with me, between the two of us we could pick out what was best.
In that case, I guess I'd better stick around with you after all.
So learn from your mistakes. Knowing you, you're repeating the same mistake over and over, am I right?
Yeah, but learn from my mistakes how?
If you just remember whether a purchase was a good one or a bad one, you'll be able to keep that in mind for next time.
If you go into things blindly every time you shop, you'll never get better at it.
Yeah, that makes sense! Like, sometimes I'll get home and realize I bought somethin' I already owned and really meant t'get something else!
Exactly. Take notes if you have to, or post something to your blog if that helps. Just so long as it helps you remember.
Oh yeah, girls blog about stuff like cosmetics, huh! Instead of recommendin' things to others, I can post a diary for myself on my blog!
That might be worth a shot. You're less likely to forget something if you've written it down.
I'm feeling kinda beat. I could go for a <Color:8>Toughness ZZ<Color:Default>.
(Looks like Riku wants a <Color:8>Toughness ZZ<Color:Default>.)
Thank you! Please come again.
Oh, this <Color:8>Black Umbrella<Color:Default> is pretty cool.
(Haruka wants that <Color:8>Black Umbrella<Color:Default>.)
I'll buy that <Color:8>Black Umbrella<Color:Default> next time.
Is there something you want?
Y'know, looking at them all on display and all, I'm kinda feelin' like I want a watch.
A watch, huh?
The one I got now I've had since high school. I figure it's time I got myself a proper one.
I see. Well, what sort would you like?
I dunno. What do you think?
One with a fancy brand name. Otherwise, what's the point of wearing a watch at all?
Y'think?
Wearing a watch isn't about telling the time. It's a fashion accessory. Something that tells other people how high-class you are.
Even if you're wearing expensive clothes, some people might think you're a cheapskate if you don't have the accessories to match.
Yeah, but that's how it works for guys, not girls, right? We should be free to pick what we feel like wearing when it comes to fashion.
If you don't care about that sort of thing, then you should just pick what you want.
Something cute. At the end of the day, you're going to see it more than anyone else, so pick something that suits you.
I see. I don't wanna get one just t'show it off. Even if it's from some famous label, I don't want some design I ain't even like.
Exactly. Plus, a man would be intimidated if a woman wore a really expensive watch.
I don't think a woman needs to worry about brands or price. It should be okay to just pick something cute to go with their outfit.
I'll do that! Thanks for the tip, Kiryu-san!
Heh. Glad I could help.
Something cheap. You just need it to tell time.
Y'really believe that!? Then I might as well just keep the one I got now. But I don't wanna look like no high school student.
If you don't like the way it looks, why not ditch the watch and wear a bracelet instead?
Well because I wanna wear one, ya know?
Most people use their cell phones to tell time nowadays. Why even bother with a watch?
Yeah, but guys can just carry 'em in their pockets. A girl puts hers in her purse, so it's a hassle to check the time.
Aw, this bites. And here I thought ya'd have some good advice on watches, Kiryu-san.
Do you know what you'd like, miss?
Oh, I want the <Color:8>Italian Women's Watch<Color:Default>! It looks totes adorbs!
(Looks like Riku's got her eye on the <Color:8>Italian Women's Watch<Color:Default>.)
Look at that <Color:8>Aji Mentaiko 240 g (Regular)<Color:Default>! Let's get some to take home!
(Haruka wants to get some <Color:8>Aji Mentaiko 240 g (Regular)<Color:Default> to take home.)
Aww, don't you want some <Color:8>Aji Mentaiko 240 g (Regular)<Color:Default>?
You know, I'm starting to get the hang of shopping in places like this.
You don't usually shop at convenience stores?
No. Before working in Kineicho, I never really had the opportunity to visit them.
No way! There's one on practically every street! Heck, what kid hasn't hit up a convenience store on their way to school?
I was always driven to school when I was a child, so I never had the opportunity to go in one.
Well, what about after you got home? You never had the urge to go shopping for some snacks?
Our servants always did the shopping whenever I needed something.
I actually never did any shopping at all until I was an adult.
Rich people sure lead different lives! It must have been cool, getting your servants to do anything you needed.
I suppose. My mother is French, so she was at quite a loss without the help of our servants.
My mother hired them to act almost as tutors, to teach her how to live the Japanese lifestyle.
Oh, I get what you mean. So does that mean they're all gone now?
Yes. They were only employed during my childhood.
Wow, so your mom's been living in Japan for a long time now.
I believe it's been close to thirty years. She's able to do anything on her own now.
I'm sure that must've taken lots of hard work.
That's a shame.
What makes you say that?
Because having other people do everything for you doesn't teach you how to fend for yourself.
At the very least, kids should be expected to help out their parents where they can. Otherwise, they grow up kinda helpless.
Quite so! The first time I went shopping on my own, I was a mess.
That's why you gotta make sure kids get to experience that while they're young!
I mean, obviously you wouldn't want to send a little kid on a shopping errand alone. Parents should follow them on the sly.
Oh, Shinada-san, you're so overprotective! I bet you'll make a splendid father one day.
You really think so? I kinda always figured I'd be a stubborn, cranky old man.
I bet you always pay by card, huh?
I... Well, yes, I do. Why, is there something wrong with that?
Oh, no. I didn't mean to upset you.
I just mean, like, if you pay by card every time you buy something, doesn't that slow you down at the register?
No, not at all. Is it not more time-consuming to go through the effort of sorting out your change after the purchase?
Nah, just put it in one of those donation boxes they have near the cash register.
Fine, I'll do that from now on! I'm sorry I'm such a cheap woman!
Er, why do I get the feeling I offended you somehow?

Let's see. I'd like some <Color:8>Makeup Remover<Color:Default>.
Do convenience stores carry that sort of thing?
(Seems that Shion-chan wants some <Color:8>Makeup Remover<Color:Default>.)
Uncle Kaz, I'd really like a <Color:8>Grilled Onigiri with Miso<Color:Default>.
(Haruka wants to have a <Color:8>Grilled Onigiri with Miso<Color:Default>.)
But I wanted a <Color:8>Grilled Onigiri with Miso<Color:Default>.
Welcome. Would you like to order?
My doctor says that I should abstain from alcohol, so I'll have a soft drink instead.
Oh, my bad. I shouldn't have brought you to a place like this. Sorry.
No, it's all right. I do enjoy alcohol quite a bit. I'm sure it wouldn't be an issue if I had only a tiny sip.
Sure, just a tiny sip! Then I'll drink the rest. Are you cool with that?
Of course, I'd be happy to!
So, what'll it be?
Hmm. <Color:8>The Macallan 30 Years<Color:Default> sounds like it would be good.
(Shion wants <Color:8>The Macallan 30 Years<Color:Default>.)
You strike me as an early riser, Shinada-san. Do you usually stay out late drinking?
Not usually. But if I've got something like a deadline to meet, I'll be up all night working on it.

Oh, really?
Such an irregular lifestyle isn't good for your health.
I make sure I get enough sleep. The sun sets earlier now, so it's pretty much already evening by the time I wake up.
Back in the day, I'd be up before sunrise for morning practice every day, but that's all behind me now.
Perhaps early to bed, early to rise is best. That way you get some healthy exposure to sunlight!
I'll try my best! I've got to improve my lifestyle first, so I don't have to keep late hours any more.
Oh. Does that mean you won't be coming by the club anymore?
Huh? No, of course I will! I'll come and see you all the time, Shion-chan!
But you won't be able to go out at night. And I'm sure you'll be focused on your job during the daytime.
Well, um... Yeesh, what should I do?
Hehe! I'm only joking! Please don't stress out about it.
Hey now, don't scare me like that! I was starting to freak out!
But that's a good sign. It's never a bad idea to re-evaluate your lifestyle.
Argh. What should I do? I feel like my life is in your hands, Shion-chan.
Does that really work? I mean, wouldn't anyone who works nights be unhealthy then?
Oh dear, you may be right. I heard that proper exposure to sunlight is a key element to healthy living.
Whoa, for real?
But then, if you can get those health benefits from somewhere else, you wouldn't really need the sunlight.
I wonder. The reasoning certainly seems sound.
I should probably look into some options myself. Maybe there are some fancy gadgets that'll even get a night owl like me nice and healthy!
I think it would be far simpler if you made a point to wake up early. Not to mention, it wouldn't cost you any money.
Aww, geez. Not only am I broke, I'm too busy trying to make money to be healthy!
I don't care if I'm unhealthy. Forcing myself to live in a way that doesn't fit me would just make me depressed in the long run.
But you need to take care of yourself in both mind and body. It won't do any good if only one of those is in good shape.
Well, what if I have to choose one or the other?
I'd go with my mind, no question.
Why is that?
I'm always working out, and thanks to sports medicine, my nutritional needs are where they need to be. I actually think about this stuff, you know.
But when it comes to my head, I can't even focus on things. And I'm speaking from personal experience here.
Ah, yes. I think I understand. When I was suffering from a shocking incident in the past, I couldn't even get myself to eat.
See? If you have no motivation, your daily routine goes out the window.
I can't have myself being like that, so I try to focus on keeping myself strong mentally.
I can see that you have! Just looking at you is enough to cheer me up, Shinada-san! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That's great!
Thank you for treating me!
Thank you very much. Please come by again.
Welcome. Oh, I'm sorry, young lady. I can't serve you alcohol. But please come by again in a few years.
Sir, I think you've had enough. You may want to ease off.
Are you a fan of tequila, sir? It's all the rage over in the US right now.
Oh yes. Many foreign celebrities are tequila fans, and Hollywood is the epicenter of this current wave of popularity.
Wow, I didn't know that. Isn't tequila pretty harsh, though? I'd figure it wouldn't really fit with traditional Japanese tastes.
Actually, the alcohol content of tequila only ranges between 35 and 55 percent. So it isn't that strong compared to vodka, which can reach up to 90 percent.
And if it's premium one hundred percent agave tequila, the alcohol processes easily, so anyone can drink it without fear of feeling sick.
(Tequila's big with celebrities, huh? Might be something to talk about at the cabaret club.)
Aww, darn it.
Huh? What's wrong?
There was somethin' here that I'd had my eye on when I came by today.
